_comment: THE archiver host-lane table (#5448 step 4). One row per lane: which box runs it, which image hosts
and provider tags it owns, the per-host rate it may use, and pages in flight.
scripts/catalog-coverage/archive-lanes-revive.sh (cron, every 10 min, on each box) starts every lane
whose `box` is this box and that has no tmux session; archive-lanes.mjs turns a row into the
archive-acquired.ts flags. tests/unit/archive-lanes-table.test.ts refuses: a rate above the host's
DOMAIN_LIMITS entry, a host in two lanes (one host = one lane = one egress address; never add an
address to raise a host's rate), an MDZ lane (the MDZ rate waits on BSB's reply, #5448), and a box
`rate` is LOWER-ONLY (capDomainLimit): a lane takes a share of a host's polite rate, never more.
Hosts other archivers also reach (archive-ocr on main reaches SBB, Gottingen, NB, Vatican,
Heidelberg) get 1/s or less here so the two together stay near the host's existing rate.
`box: mac` lanes are listed for completeness and started by nothing on the boxes.

lanes.name: heidelberg
lanes.note: Was hand-listed in /etc/sourcelibrary/archive-lanes.conf (campaign acquisition-wave-2026-10); now every Heidelberg book. iiif.bodleian.ox.ac.uk: the 82 Bodleian manuscripts the portal served through its dead iiif-proxy.cgi now point at Bodleian directly (#5448).

lanes.name: vatican
lanes.note: 0.1/s as in the /etc conf it replaces.

lanes.name: goettingen
lanes.note: SUB Gottingen. A manifest-only book's lane is its manifest host until its ledger records the image host, so both are listed.

lanes.name: nb-norway
lanes.note: Nasjonalbiblioteket: manifests on api.nb.no, images on www.nb.no.

lanes.name: e-rara
lanes.note: e-rara 403s main's address (tier-A import, 2026-10-25) and archive-ocr excludes it; 200 from l7a the same day. 1/s, half its table rate, because the hourly cron on main also reaches it.

lanes.name: gallica
lanes.note: gallica.bnf.fr 403s datacenter addresses; the same IIIF image is served by openapi.bnf.fr (Image API 3.0). Lane chosen by the page's gallica.bnf.fr URL, fetched from openapi.bnf.fr.

lanes.name: ia-lazy
lanes.note: Manifest-only IA books from the item _jp2.zip when the canvas→member mapping is proven (ia-zip-ledger.mjs), else per page over IIIF. --ia-zip needs opj_decompress + unzip; on a box without them every book falls back before any request . On gex45 (62 GB, x86): on l7a this lane's node reached 4.4 GB RSS on 51 MP IA leaves and the box went global-OOM at 2026-10-26 00:13:59, taking another service's runner with it. Live on gex45 since 2026-10-26 08:00 (revive cron + libopenjp2-tools/unzip installed from the laptop session): exact mapping, 1.35 pages/s at 2 in flight, bound by JP2 decode + re-encode on a box with 20 cores idle, so 8 in flight. The zip route runs page_concurrency decoders; watch the heartbeat's rss (node only; each opj_decompress child adds ~0.6 GB on a 51 MP leaf). Materialized IA books stay with archive-bulk.mjs (item zips, scheduler on main).

lanes.name: harvard
lanes.note: Harvard's ELB 429s every Hetzner address (archive-ocr note, 2026-05-25); archive-harvard.mjs runs on the Mac. Listed so the table names every host; no box starts it.
